test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 17 Aug, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT included in the category of Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nehruvian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nehruvian** is NOT included in the** category of Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• **The Directive Principles of State Policy **in India are categorized into several groups: **Economic and Socialistic, Political and Administrative, Justice and Legal, Environmental, Protection of Monuments, Peace and Security. **
 
• These principles serve as guidelines for the governance of the country by the government of India. 
 
• While not enforceable by any court, they are deemed fundamental in the administration of the nation, making it the responsibility of the State to incorporate these principles into the formulation of laws to establish a fair society. 
 
• These principles draw inspiration from similar directives outlined in the Constitution of Ireland, which pertain to social justice, economic welfare, foreign policy, and legal and administrative affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In 1928, the **Nehru Commission, **which included representatives from all Indian political parties, put forward constitutional reforms for India.
 
• These reforms advocated for dominion status for India, elections conducted through universal suffrage, and the assurance of fundamental rights.
 
• Additionally, the proposals aimed to provide representation for religious and ethnic minorities while also restraining the powers of the government.
 
• In 1931, the Indian National Congress, the predominant political party at the time, adopted resolutions affirming its commitment to safeguarding fundamental civil rights.
 
• Furthermore, the Congress pledged to promote socio-economic rights such as establishing a minimum wage and abolishing untouchability and serfdom. These resolutions demonstrated the Congress's dedication to the principles of socialism.
